target.title: Decoding Vowels and Consonants in Spoken and Imagined Words Using Electrocorticographic Signals in Humans

read.pdf: No PDF supplied; figure captions Fig. 1–7 and Tables 1–7 in text.txt read

entries.text: The cohort comprised eight patients with intractable epilepsy undergoing temporary subdural electrode placement for seizure localization.
entries.condition: Clinical cohort; electrode placement was for seizure localization before surgical resection.

entries.text: The cohort included two men and six women; electrode locations varied, and only subject G had right-hemisphere coverage.
entries.condition: Subjects A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and I; all subjects except G had left-hemisphere grids.

entries.text: Each participant had a 48- or 64-contact subdural grid over frontal, parietal, and temporal regions.
entries.condition: Grid placement was clinically determined and varied across subjects; electrodes were 2.3 mm exposed diameter and 1 cm apart.

entries.text: The closed stimulus set contained 36 English monosyllabic CVC words built from four vowels and nine consonant pairs; these were real words, not pseudowords.
entries.condition: Vowels /ε/, /æ/, /i:/, /u:/; consonant pairs /b_t/, /c_n/, /h_d/, /l_d/, /m_n/, /p_p/, /r_d/, /s_t/, /t_n/.

entries.text: Each displayed word remained on screen for 4 seconds, followed by a 0.5-second blank interval; participants repeated it overtly or covertly.
entries.unit: seconds per presentation; seconds blank interval
entries.condition: Separate overt and covert runs; word stimuli presented visually.

entries.text: Each subject completed 2–7 runs per task condition, with 36 trials per run and 140 trials per condition on average.
entries.condition: Overt and covert word repetition; run counts varied by subject.

entries.text: All eight subjects performed overt repetition; six subjects (A–F) performed covert repetition, with subject-specific trial totals reported as 72–216 overt and 72–252 covert.
entries.value: 8 overt subjects; 6 covert subjects; 72–216 overt trials; 72–252 covert trials
entries.condition: Overt mean 140 trials and covert mean 126 trials; covert subset A, B, C, D, E, F.
entries.quote: All eight subjects participated in the experiments using overt word repetition; a subset of six subjects (A, B, C, D, E, F) participated in experiments using covert word repetition.

entries.text: The average trial totals were 140 for overt and 126 for covert speech.
entries.condition: Overt range 72–216; covert range 72–252; subjects repeated visually prompted words.

entries.text: ECoG and microphone signals were bandpass filtered at 0.15–500 Hz and digitized at 1200 Hz.
entries.unit: Hz filter band; Hz sampling rate
entries.condition: Signals acquired via BCI2000 and g.USBamp; only a subset had microphone recordings.

entries.text: After visual channel inspection and removal of noisy or non-ECoG channels, 47–64 channels remained for analysis.
entries.condition: Channel screening was performed per dataset; excluded examples included ground/reference channels and broken connections.
entries.quote: which left 47–64 channels for our analyses.

entries.text: Signals were rereferenced with common average reference; spectra used 333-ms windows stepped every 50 ms and an AR model of order 25.
entries.unit: ms window; ms step; AR order
entries.condition: Per electrode; preceding 333 ms converted every 50 ms; model order empirically determined.

entries.text: Spectral power was averaged in mu, beta, and high-gamma bands; high gamma excluded 116–124 Hz.
entries.condition: Per channel; spectral amplitudes initially computed from 0–200 Hz in 2-Hz bins.

entries.text: Four feature sets, including local motor potential, covered 500–2500 ms after stimulus onset and yielded 136 features per trial.
entries.unit: feature sets; ms post-stimulus; ms window; ms step; features/trial
entries.condition: 136 features comprise four sets with 34 samples per set; LMP is a running average of the raw signal.

entries.text: MRMR ranked features separately for each channel and task/target analysis; the top 35 consonant or 40 vowel features fed a Naive Bayes classifier.
entries.condition: Feature ranking was separate for overt/covert and vowel/consonant analyses; classification was trial-level.
entries.quote: Then, separately for each channel and analysis (overt or covert speech, vowels or consonants), we ranked the ECoG features using the MRMR (Maximum Relevance and Minimum Redundancy) criterion

entries.text: Accuracy used ten-fold cross-validation, training on nine folds and testing on the remaining fold; no independent external test cohort is described.
entries.condition: The paper describes folds within each dataset; subject- and run-grouping details are not specified.
entries.quote: the parameters of the Bayes classifier were determined from 9/10 th of the dataset as training set and tested on the remaining 1/10 th test set.

entries.text: Consonant accuracy averaged results over all 126 four-of-nine consonant-pair combinations, reporting the average for the best location.
entries.condition: Consonant-pair groups compared with four-vowel classification; ten-fold cross-validation for each combination.

entries.text: The authors used 25% chance accuracy for four-class vowel and matched four-class consonant-pair classification.
entries.condition: Four categories in each matched-group classifier; consonant groups sampled from nine possible pairs.

entries.text: Mean vowel accuracy at the best location was 40.7±2.7% for overt and 37.5±5.9% for covert speech.
entries.condition: Across subjects; overt n=8 and covert n=6; individual-location performance; four-vowel classification with ten-fold CV.
entries.quote: The average classification accuracies for decoding vowels across all subjects were 40.7±2.7% (overt speech) and 37.5±5.9% (covert speech) (see Figure 4 and supplementary material Video 1 ).

entries.text: Mean consonant-pair accuracy at the best location was 40.6±8.3% for overt and 36.3±9.7% for covert speech.
entries.condition: Across subjects; overt n=8 and covert n=6; best location; four matched consonant-pair classes averaged across all combinations.
entries.quote: For decoding consonants, the average classification accuracies across all subjects for best location were 40.6±8.3% (overt speech) and 36.3±9.7% (covert speech) (see Figure 4 ).

entries.text: For the best class in each task, the paper reports 39% and 43% for /u:/ overt/covert and 33% and 28% for R_D overt/covert.
entries.condition: Best-performing vowel /u:/ and consonant pair R_D; averaged across subjects; four-class matched groups; overt/covert order as stated.

entries.text: The Table 4 diagonal gives 32.9±12.5% for correct R_D classification during overt speech.
entries.condition: Overt consonant decoding; correct row R_D and predicted column R_D; composite over all 126 four-of-nine combinations.

entries.text: The Table 5 diagonal gives 27.8±16.9% for correct R_D classification during covert speech.
entries.condition: Covert consonant decoding; correct row R_D and predicted column R_D; composite over all 126 four-of-nine combinations.

entries.text: The Table 6 diagonal gives 38.91±7.68% for correct /u:/ classification during overt speech.
entries.condition: Overt vowel decoding; correct row /u:/ and predicted column /u:/.

entries.text: The Table 7 diagonal gives 42.72±9.35% for correct /u:/ classification during covert speech.
entries.condition: Covert vowel decoding; correct row /u:/ and predicted column /u:/.

entries.text: The authors report above-chance performance in both overt and covert speech, with significant per-subject results for most task/phoneme combinations.
entries.value: overt vowels: all 8, p<0.004; overt consonants: 7/8, prose p<0.0022; covert vowels: 5/6, p<0.007; covert consonants: 4/6, p<0.03
entries.condition: Four-class classification; parameterized bootstrap resampling with 10,000 repetitions; p exceptions: H for overt consonants, B for covert vowels, C and E for covert consonants.
entries.quote: In particular, for overt speech, accuracies were significant in all subjects (p<0.004) for vowels and in most subjects (7/8 subjects, p<0.0022) for consonants

entries.text: The prose reports overt-consonant significance as p<0.0022, while Table 3 prints p<0.022 except subject H.
entries.value: p<0.0022 in prose; p<0.022 in Table 3
entries.condition: Overt consonant decoding; 7 of 8 subjects reported significant in the prose, with H excepted in Table 3.

entries.text: The authors claim this is the first demonstration of vowel and consonant decoding from spoken or imagined monosyllabic words using human ECoG, alongside cortical localization.
entries.value: first demonstration, as claimed by authors
entries.condition: Vowels and consonants embedded in spoken or imagined monosyllabic words; human ECoG.
entries.quote: for the first time that it is possible to decode vowels and consonants that are embedded in spoken or imagined monosyllabic words from ECoG signals in humans,

entries.text: The authors claim independent decoding of vowels and consonant pairs across spoken and imagined words, and say no earlier study had demonstrated this task.
entries.condition: Word-embedded phonemes; ECoG signals; closed vocabulary and four-class matched-group evaluation.

entries.text: The authors describe the reported accuracies as substantially better than the 25% chance level.
entries.condition: Four-class vowel and matched consonant-pair classification; per-subject ten-fold cross-validation.

entries.text: The authors report different discriminative cortical patterns for vowels and consonants, with overt-task information in motor, premotor, Broca, and posterior temporal regions.
entries.condition: Cortical maps built from per-electrode classification accuracy; covert maps were described as smaller foci and more variable across subjects.

entries.text: The reshuffling analysis found no significant map overlap between vowels and consonants (overt p>0.26; covert p=1) or between overt and covert speech (vowels p>0.94; consonants p>0.37), with a subject-A consonant exception at p<0.05.
entries.condition: Spatial overlap of discriminative cortical maps; individual-subject and pooled analyses; subject A exception for individual consonant-map comparison.

entries.text: Mean decoding accuracies were described as similar for overt and covert speech; the paired tests found no significant differences between overt/covert or vowel/consonant accuracies.
entries.condition: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; eight overt subjects and six covert subjects.

entries.text: The authors say it is unclear whether the findings generalize beyond the word-repetition task used.
entries.condition: The study tested prompted overt and covert repetition of a fixed word set.

entries.text: The authors call for improved accuracy and extension to more vowel/consonant categories; they suggest combining information across locations rather than using individual locations alone.
entries.value: more categories and multi-location information proposed
entries.condition: Current reported decoding used each electrode location separately.

entries.text: The paper does not report random seeds or state whether cross-validation folds were stratified, randomized, grouped by run/session, or repeated with independent partitions.
entries.condition: Ten-fold cross-validation is specified, but the fold-generation procedure and seed are not.
entries.quote: For each vowel, the classifier was constructed and evaluated using ten-fold cross-validation.

entries.text: It is not stated whether MRMR feature ranking, feature-count choice, or best-location selection was repeated inside each training fold or nested within cross-validation.
entries.condition: The manuscript describes feature ranking and feature selection before explaining the ten-fold classifier evaluation; no separate validation set is described.
entries.quote: Then, separately for each channel and analysis (overt or covert speech, vowels or consonants), we ranked the ECoG features using the MRMR (Maximum Relevance and Minimum Redundancy) criterion

entries.text: Normalization or standardization of classifier inputs, and whether any scaling parameters were estimated only on training folds, are not specified.
entries.condition: The paper labels example spectrograms normalized but gives no classifier-feature normalization procedure.

entries.text: No held-out-speaker evaluation or cross-subject transfer test is reported; performance is evaluated using folds of the study datasets.
entries.condition: Per-subject channel analyses and ten-fold CV; no independent participant test set described.

entries.text: For covert trials, the target label comes from the displayed word and instruction to imagine speaking it; no independent verification of imagined content is described.
entries.condition: Covert word-repetition trials; no acoustic speech signal is available to verify the imagined response.
entries.quote: In separate experimental runs, ECoG was recorded during two different conditions: overt or covert word repetition in response to visual word stimuli.

entries.text: No language model or other linguistic decoding aid is reported; the described output is the vowel or consonant-pair class from a Naive Bayes classifier.
entries.condition: Closed-set four-class vowel or consonant-pair classification.

entries.text: No online or unconstrained communication deployment is evaluated; the supplementary imagined-vowel demonstration was produced offline from one cross-validation fold for subject D.
entries.condition: Offline video example using visual prompts and 500–2500-ms ECoG features; not a prospective real-time test.
entries.quote: This example was produced offline based on results from one cross-validation fold from subject D.

entries.text: The paper provides no linked analysis repository or training/evaluation scripts; the cited AFNI SUMA code concerns the cortical brain model and its linked page is unavailable.
entries.condition: The AFNI SUMA URL cited in Sec. 2.4 returned HTTP 404; no repository README or experiment scripts were available to inspect.

entries.text: Although the maps differed statistically, the authors note that this does not rule out shared cortical commonalities; overt vowel and consonant maps shared premotor and middle-temporal regions.
entries.condition: Cortical discriminative maps for overt and covert vowel/consonant tasks.

entries.text: The authors present the findings as a possible basis for speech-based BCI communication with little training, not as a demonstrated deployed system.
entries.condition: Future implication from prompted overt/covert word-repetition experiments; no online deployment evaluation.
entries.quote: Thus, the results presented here may ultimately lead to speech-based BCI systems that may provide effective communication with only little training.

entries.text: The cortical-map overlap null used 1,000,000 electrode-position reshuffles to build its surrogate distribution.
entries.condition: For spatial overlap of two cortical discriminative maps; electrode positions for one condition were randomly reshuffled.

entries.text: For spatial maps, individual-subject analyses thresholded z-scores at 1.64 (p=0.05); pooled maps used z=2, and Fig. 5 labels z=2 as p=0.0023.
entries.condition: Individual-subject and pooled cortical discriminative-map analyses; Fig. 5 caption reports p=0.0023 at z=2.
entries.quote: Color gives z-scores indicating how much better accuracy at the respective location was compared to chance (p-value: 0.0023 at a z-score of 2).

questions.q: What are the headline decoding results, and under which evaluation conditions were they obtained?
questions.answer: The reported means are 40.7±2.7% and 37.5±5.9% for overt/covert vowels, and 40.6±8.3% and 36.3±9.7% for overt/covert consonant pairs. Evaluation used four-class tasks, per-subject ten-fold cross-validation, eight overt participants and six covert participants; no external test cohort is described.

questions.q: Does the study establish general-purpose imagined-speech communication or online deployment?
questions.answer: No. It tests prompted covert repetition of a displayed word from a fixed vocabulary, reports no online deployment, and explicitly says generalization beyond word repetition is unclear.

questions.q: Which evaluation details are missing for reproducibility and generalization claims?
questions.answer: The paper omits fold assignment and random seeds, whether feature selection and best-location selection were nested within folds, classifier-feature normalization, and held-out-speaker evaluation. It also gives no independent verification of covert imagined-word content.
